_comment: Machine-readable registry for BF16-in / BF16-out GEMM on NPU2. Single source of truth for tile configs + measured performance; the GEMM_bf16_in_bf16_out.md tables mirror this. Consumed by llama via kernel_registry/registry_lookup.py gemm_config(). tile is a named object {tile_m, tile_k_l2, tile_k_l1, tile_n} (self-describing). herd 8x4. Two precision tiers: 'high' (fused-cast / drain = f32 accumulate + single cast, 9.3-9.9e-3) and 'low' (direct-codegen per-L2-tile bf16 truncation, 1.0-1.9e-2). best.high = faster of fused-cast/drain (M*K*N>=4e9 -> fused-cast cross-over). fused-cast gflops INCLUDE the cast launch.

shapes.used_by: SmolVLA connector proj (vision->LLM, K=12288 very large, M=64 very small)
shapes._note: Connector projection between the vision encoder and the LLM. M=64 is tiny and K=12288 is very large. M=64 forces tile_m=16 (mm.o static_assert m%(2*8)==0 rejects tile_m=8) and herd_m=4 (tile_m*herd_m=64=M; tile_m=16/herd_m=8=128 > M fails the m%(tile_m*herd_m)==0 assert). MKN=7.5e8 < 4e9 -> drain. K=12288 is NOT a placement blocker -- just 48 reduction tiles at tile_k_l2=256; PLACES and PASSES cleanly at 9.450e-3, abs_err max 3.662e-4. NO CPU fallback needed. TILE_N=240: N=960=4*240 and 240 satisfies the mmul t=8 constraint (n%(2*t)==0). WHY 240 AND NOT 80: the measured tile_n sweep at herd 4x4 (2026-07-27) is strongly non-flat -- 16:3352us, 48:1347us, 80:890us, 240:667-713us. tile_n=240 is 1.33x FASTER than the tile_n=80 this row originally carried, at BIT-IDENTICAL accuracy (both 9.450e-3, abs_err max 3.662e-4). The old 80 came from the generic 'N not 512-aligned -> shrink TILE_N' habit (4*80=320 | 960), which is the wrong instinct for this tiny-M/huge-K shape: fewer, larger N-tiles amortize the weight DMA far better. tile_k_l2 is nearly inert across {128,256,384} (686/689/672us; 384 marginally best); tile_k_l2 >= 512 FAILS TO COMPILE (L1 over-allocation) -- an earlier revision of this note claimed 512/768 were flat-but-working, which was wrong. 16 TILES IS THE HARD CEILING, and it is NOT costing performance. The full (tile_m,herd_m,tile_n,herd_n) grid was enumerated under tile_m%16==0, tile_n%16==0, M%(tile_m*herd_m)==0, N%(tile_n*herd_n)==0, herd_m<=8, herd_n<=4: 4x4 is the maximum reachable (tile_n=120 would allow herd_n=8 but violates n%16, verified by compile failure). Padding M 64->128 to fill the full 8x4 herd was MEASURED and is SLOWER in wall-clock (975us vs 892us at tile_n=80; 734us vs 667-713us at tile_n=240) -- the doubled GFLOPS is pure padding waste. ROOT CAUSE: this GEMM is WEIGHT-DMA-BOUND, not tile-bound. B is 12288*960*2 = 23.6 MB vs A 1.57 MB + C 0.12 MB, i.e. 93% of traffic and independent of M; 25.3 MB in ~890us ~= 28 GB/s, at the DMA ceiling. Confirmed two ways: halving K halves latency (892->518us), and the herd_m sweep at 4/8/16 tiles (7358/1668/888us) is near-linear then saturates. Extra tiles have no extra bandwidth to consume.

shapes.used_by: SmolVLA action expert QK^T on ODD (cross-attn) layers: group-batched S = Q_group @ K_h^T against the frozen 241-token prefix, padded to 256
shapes._note: M=192 (GQA group 3 x 64 padded action tokens) admits only three (tile_m, herd_m) pairs under mm.o's tile_m%16==0, run.py's M%(tile_m*herd_m)==0, and the single-M-launch-iteration rule M//tile_m//herd_m==1: 32x6, 48x4, 64x3. Measured: 32x6 and 48x4 are within noise of each other, 64x3 is consistently slowest (only 12 of 32 tiles). shapes.used_by: SmolVLA Q/O proj (emb=960; drain tile_m=32, TILE_N=80, HERD_N=4; K=960 tile_k_l2=320)
SmolVLA vision q/k/v/out_proj (SigLIP, seq=1024, hidden=768) + patch-embedding-as-GEMM (im2col, same shape)
shapes._note: SigLIP vision encoder. seq=1024, hidden=768. M=1024 -> drain tile_m=32 runs 1024/(32*8)=4 M-launch iterations; the standalone drain harness handles multi-iteration M correctly (verified PASS at 9.465e-3), the mm.o multi-iteration garbage bug does NOT apply to this single-launch drain path. N=768 not 512-aligned -> TILE_N=96 (4*96=384 | 768). K=768 tile_k_l2=384 (768/384=2). MKN=6e8 < 4e9 -> drain. abs_err max 1.709e-3 is covered by rtol*|ref| (not a near-zero element) -> PASSES high-precision.

Vision MLP up-projection (fc1). N=3072=4*128*6 -> stock TILE_N=128. K=768 tile_k_l2=256 (768/256=3). Same wide-N Gate/Up near-zero atol edge as every Qwen sibling: high-precision drain computes the in-tier result (mean_rel_L1=9.428e-3, 4195 GFLOPS @ tile_m=32/tk2=256/tn128) but the harness element-wise gate trips on a near-zero-reference element (abs_err 1.953e-3 > high-prec atol=1.5e-3, rtol*|ref|~0). The low-precision direct path PASSES (atol=4e-3, 1.089e-2). best.high points at the numerically-correct drain datapath; best.low at the harness-passing direct path.

Vision MLP down-projection (fc2). N=768 not 512-aligned -> TILE_N=96 (4*96=384 | 768). K=3072 tile_k_l2=384 (3072/384=8). MKN=2.4e9 < 4e9 -> drain. Down-proj-class (large K, small N) is the fast one, clean high-precision at 9.423e-3, abs_err max 8.5e-4 (no near-zero edge).
Thin N=128=4*32. drain TILE_M=32 TILE_N=32 HERD_N=4 (full 8x4 herd required).

Non-512-aligned N=896=128*7. HERD_N=1 (TILE_N=128) fails at runtime (qds_device::wait unexpected command state) — fused-cast/drain paths assume the 8x4 array. Working config keeps HERD_N=4 with TILE_N=32 (4*32=128 | 896); drain (tile_m=32) places, fused-cast tile_m=64 over-allocates L1.

N=4864=256*19; TILE_N=64 HERD_N=4 (4*64=256 | 4864). High-precision fused-cast computes the in-tier result (9.4e-3) but the harness gate trips on 2 near-zero-reference elements (abs_err ~1.6-1.9e-3 > high-prec atol=1.5e-3). The low-precision direct path PASSES (atol=4e-3, 1.11e-2). Same artifact as Qwen3-0.6B Gate/Up. best.low = harness-passing direct path.
auto picks drain; fused-cast at tile_m=64 over-allocates L1 (compile fail) for this thin N, drain (tile_m=32) is the working high-precision method.

High-precision fused-cast/drain compute the in-tier result (mean_rel_L1=9.4e-3) but the harness element-wise gate trips on one near-zero-reference element (abs_err~1.7e-3 > high-prec atol=1.5e-3). The low-precision direct path PASSES (atol=4e-3). best.high points at the numerically-correct fused-cast; best.low at the harness-passing direct path.
thin N=256=4*64 -> TILE_N=64 HERD_N=4. MKN=8e8 < 4e9 -> drain (TILE_M=32); fused-cast over-allocates L1 at this thin N.
N=1536=512*3 divisible by default 4*TILE_N=512 -> stock TILE_N=128 HERD_N=4 (no shrink). K=1536 tile_k_l2=256 (1536/256=6). MKN=4.8e9 >= 4e9 -> fused-cast.

N=8960=256*35 -> TILE_N=64 HERD_N=4. High-precision fused-cast (TILE_M=64 TILE_N=64) over-allocates L1 -> compile fail; low-precision direct PASSES but only with TILE_K_L2=128 (1536/128=12; tile_k_l2=256 also compile-fails). Same Gate/Up tier-down as Qwen3-0.6B / Qwen2.5-0.5B. best.low = harness-passing direct path.

shapes._note: N=6144=512*12 divisible by default 4*TILE_N=512 -> stock TILE_N=128 HERD_N=4 (1024-aligned, no shrink). K=2048 tile_k_l2=256 (2048/256=8); tile_k_l2=512 BD-exhausts at this N (aie.dma_bd unassigned IDs). MKN=2.6e10 >= 4e9 -> fused-cast. No near-zero atol artifact on this run (mean_rel_L1=9.7e-3, abs_err max=1.2e-3 < high-prec atol=1.5e-3) -> PASSES high-precision directly.

N=11008=256*43 -> TILE_N=64 HERD_N=4 (4*64=256 | 11008). High-precision fused-cast AND low-prec direct at tile_k_l2=256 BOTH fail aiecc: DMA stride 2818048 (=tile_k_l2*N) exceeds the [1:1048576] aie.dma_bd range. low-prec direct with TILE_K_L2=128 PASSES at atol=4e-3. Same Gate/Up tier-down family as all Qwen siblings; root cause here is the DMA stride range, not L1.

N=9728=256*38=512*19 -> stock TILE_N=128 HERD_N=4 OK. fused-cast/direct at tile_k_l2>=128 FAIL aiecc: DMA stride tile_k_l2*N exceeds [1:1048576] (256*9728=2490368, 128*9728=1245184). High-precision fused-cast PASSES at tile_k_l2=64 (64*9728=622592 < limit), 5528 GFLOPS @ 9.8e-3 -- strictly better than the low-prec direct path (4397 @ 1.35e-2), unlike the Qwen2.5-3B/1.5B wide-N Gate/Up siblings which had to drop to low-precision. best.high=fused-cast(tile_k_l2=64).
N=2560=512*5 -> stock TILE_N=128 HERD_N=4. K=4096 tile_k_l2=256 (4096/256=16); tile_k_l2=512 DMA-stride 512*2560=1310720 > limit -> compile fail. MKN=2.1e10 -> fused-cast.
N=2048 -> stock TILE_N=128 HERD_N=4. K=6144 reduction tile_k_l2=256 (6144/256=24). MKN=2.6e10 -> fused-cast. PASSES high-precision (mean_rel_L1=9.7e-3, abs_err max=7.3e-4).
N=1536 -> stock TILE_N=128. K=8960 reduction tile_k_l2=256 (8960/256=35). MKN=2.8e10 -> fused-cast.
N=2560=512*5 -> stock TILE_N=128. K=9728=256*38 reduction tile_k_l2=256. MKN=5.1e10 -> fused-cast, PASSES high-precision at 9.8e-3.
N=2048=512*4 -> stock TILE_N=128 HERD_N=4. K=11008=256*43 reduction tile_k_l2=256. MKN=4.6e10 >= 4e9 -> fused-cast, PASSES high-precision directly at 9.8e-3.

N=2048=512*4 -> stock TILE_N=128 HERD_N=4. K=2560=256*10 -> tile_k_l2=256, DMA stride 256*2048=524288 < 1048576. Tiles inherited from the same-K Qwen3-4B 2560x4096 entry; mean_rel_L1 measured on NPU2, gflops carried over from that entry (not independently swept).

Tiles inherited from that entry; mean_rel_L1 measured on NPU2, gflops carried over (not independently swept).

fused-cast._note: tile_k_l2=128 swept on NPU2 through the prefill build path (registry -> _build_gemm_module -> stitch_elf): 4849 GF/s vs 4516 at 64 and 4143 at 32, identical mean_rel_L1. 256 fails to compile, so 128 is the ceiling at N=10240 -- the old tile_k_l2*N <= 1048576 rule was one step too conservative. The sibling 2560x9728 entry still carries the inherited 64 and has not been re-swept.
